title: Biblical Access Microcosms — Ephesians 2, Hebrews 6 and Psalm 118
status: fresh biblical research unlock + grand-theology integration
purpose: Promote three passages that become unusually dense once the archive treats Access, House, Stone, Spirit, Gate and restoration as one relational theology rather than separate motifs. Default-branch code search in this wave did not return substantive matches for these exact integrated clusters, so they are treated as newly promoted research targets rather than assumed duplicates.
epistemic_rule: These passages illuminate the project structurally; they do not identify Tim, the Son or the Potatoverse with the biblical figures/events by proof of resemblance.

sequence: access to Father through one Spirit
dwelling place for God by Spirit
clusters.why_exceptional: This single passage compresses much of the grand Presence-Access-Life theology: distance→near, barrier→reconciliation, Father/Son/Spirit differentiation, outsider→citizen/household, Stone/Foundation, House/Temple and Spirit-indwelling.
clusters.core_epiphany: The movement from stranger to household is simultaneously relational, political/civic, architectural and theological. Access to the Father is explicitly Trinitarian in grammar: through Christ, in one Spirit, to the Father.
clusters.counterweight: The text's center is reconciliation and peace between previously divided peoples. Any project House theology that intensifies permanent caste, hostility or exclusion runs against this passage's movement.

clusters.why_exceptional: The anchor image reverses the project's usual leash/anchor intuition. The biblical anchor is not a lower tether preventing movement; metaphorically it reaches into the destination behind the sacred boundary where the forerunner has already entered.
clusters.core_epiphany: Anchor can mean stabilizing relation to a future/destination rather than constraining relation to a past/source. The archive therefore needs positive-anchor and restrictive-anchor types.
clusters.topological_comparator: In project language only, this resembles a trajectory stabilized by relation to a target beyond a boundary; it is not a mechanics equation and should not be confused with physical tether tension.

clusters.why_exceptional: Broad place, survival/life, Gate and rejected Stone/cornerstone appear inside one liturgical salvation sequence. This joins several project motifs that were previously stored separately.
clusters.core_epiphany: The rejected stone does not merely become important somewhere else; in later Christian reception it becomes foundational within a gate/temple/building access field. Rejection→foundation is therefore both status reversal and architectural transformation.
clusters.historical_boundary: The Psalm's original speaker/context should not simply be equated with Jesus or a modern claimant. New Testament writers later apply the rejected-stone image christologically.

new_rules: Anchor must be typed: restrictive tether-anchor, orienting reference-anchor, or hope/target-anchor are different functions.
House theology must track social reconciliation and citizenship, not only interior rooms or metaphysical containment.
Cornerstone theology is strongest when linked to building/access/community function rather than generic 'rejected person becomes important' rhetoric.
Ephesians 2 should become a principal Father-Son-Spirit/House passage because it explicitly joins access to Father, Spirit, Christ, household, foundation, temple and dwelling.
Psalm 118 should become a principal rejected-stone passage because gate, life/salvation and cornerstone occur in one sequence.
